title: dynamic-quantizer-cache-presets-autotune
author: Nina Kaur
release_notes: Introduces a safe dynamic quantization tuner and workload-aware cache presets. The tuner profiles short live windows and recommends/apply quantization presets that trade minimal quality for cost savings. Cache presets adjust prefix/KV cache aggressive settings per workload to reduce token compute. Feature gated behind Optimize.autotune with rollout toggles; no breaking changes.
description: Motivation: teams need automatic, low-risk levers to reduce per-token costs without manual trial-and-error. This PR implements two complementary automations: 1) a dynamic quantization tuner that profiles a short warmup window and suggests or applies QuantProfiles (8-bit/4-bit safe paths) based on model, seq-length distribution, and expected quality delta; 2) workload-aware cache presets that tune prefix/KV cache retention and aggressive prefix matching to surface higher reuse for latency-sensitive bursts while falling back to conservative defaults for tail-heavy workloads. Summary of changes: added a new pkg/quant tuner that runs lightweight microbenchmarks against a shadow model in a FIFO worker, emits candidate QuantProfiles with expected token-savings and estimated quality impact, and persists profiles to the model registry; added pkg/cache presets and a small policy engine that consumes traffic telemetry to choose from presets (conservative, balanced, aggressive) per-route; integrated both automations into Redwood Optimize and the runtime routing so presets can be applied per-deployment via feature flags or rollout policies. Implementation notes: quant tuner performs short A/B shadow runs on 200 requests sampled over a 5-minute window; it uses KL-divergence + heuristic scoring to avoid changes where output drift > configured threshold; quantized variants are validated with existing eval harness (reranking and summary prompt sets) before promotion; cache presets are implemented as policy + small state machine that adjusts cache TTL and prefix-match thresholds and records per-token cost deltas for the rollout monitor. CLI and Console: added optimize autotune CLI flags (redwood optimize apply-autotune --deployment-id) and a Console toggle with a preview UI showing estimated monthly savings and quality risk. Observability: new metrics redwood_quant_tuner_candidates, redwood_quant_apply_rate, redwood_cache_preset_chosen, and cost_delta_by_deployment; traces include tuner-run-id and candidate-id. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to internal beta customers for two weeks, followed by staged enablement across Dedicated pools with opt-out. Backwards compatibility: all changes are behind toggles and default to current behavior; quantizer will not replace user-pinned model variants. Tests: unit tests for tuner scoring and preset selection are included; integration tests exercise a simulated traffic trace validating expected reduction in cost-per-token without quality regressions; e2e harness added a synthetic workload to run on PR builders. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-1028) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] CI green - [x] console + CLI UX - [x] docs updated - [x] migration/rollout plan added Links: design notes https://linear.app/redwood/ENG-1028/quantization-autotuner and dashboard mock https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/optimize-autotune. Files of note: pkg/quant/tuner.go, pkg/quant/profile_store.go, pkg/cache/presets.go, pkg/optimize/handler.go, cmd/redwood-optimize/main.go, webapp/src/components/OptimizeAutotunePreview.tsx, docs/ops/quant-autotune.md, tests/e2e/quant-cache-autotune.test.ts, scripts/profiler-runner.sh. Migration: no DB migrations; registry entries are additive. Security: quantizer runs in a sandboxed worker with no access to customer payloads outside sampling policy. Performance: initial internal beta shows ~18-23% CPU/GPU token cost reduction on medium seq-length conversational workloads and negligible signal loss on the eval suites used during validation.
